title: Valentine success GIF slideshow + custom love text

requirements.summary: Replace the success-screen static meme image with a looping two-GIF timed slideshow (img3.gif then img1.gif) referenced as frontend static assets.
acceptanceCriteria: From the main Valentine prompt screen, clicking the “Yes” button navigates to/shows the success view.
The success view displays a looping slideshow using the two uploaded GIFs: img3.gif and img1.gif.
The slideshow shows exactly one GIF at a time and automatically transitions to the next on a timer; after the second GIF it loops back to the first.
The GIFs are referenced as static assets from the frontend (not served via the backend), and render correctly in production build.

file_operations.description: Add the uploaded GIF asset img3.gif to the app’s static public assets so it can be referenced by the success view in production builds.
Add the uploaded GIF asset img1.gif to the app’s static public assets so it can be referenced by the success view in production builds.
Create a small React component that cycles through a provided list of GIF src strings on a fixed timer and loops back to the beginning (show exactly one GIF at a time).
Replace the current static meme with the new GifSlideshow component configured to loop through /assets/img3.gif then /assets/img1.gif on a timer; ensure the slideshow area is centered and responsive.

requirements.summary: Show the exact text “I love you Himani Chauhan” beneath the GIF slideshow on the success screen, readable on mobile and desktop.
acceptanceCriteria: The success screen includes the text “I love you Himani Chauhan” exactly (spelling and spacing as shown).
The text appears beneath the GIF slideshow and remains readable on both mobile and desktop screen sizes.

file_operations.description: Add the exact string “I love you Himani Chauhan” as a dedicated text element placed directly beneath the GIF slideshow container; apply responsive typography so it remains readable on mobile and desktop.

requirements.summary: Maintain the existing Valentine prompt page behavior: question + Yes/No buttons, and No clicks progressively enlarge the Yes button without layout regressions.
acceptanceCriteria: The prompt page still shows the Valentine question and both “Yes” and “No” buttons.
Clicking “No” continues to increase the “Yes” button size progressively, capped as currently implemented.
No new regressions: the prompt page remains usable on mobile and desktop (buttons remain tappable/clickable and not clipped off-screen).

file_operations.description: Preserve the current No-click counter and Yes-button scaling logic while adding small responsiveness safeguards (e.g., centering/spacing and overflow handling) so the scaled Yes button remains tappable and not clipped on smaller screens.
